title: Cipla Recalls UTI Treatment Drug Fosfomycin Tromethamine Granules in US

contentHtml:
New Delhi: Cipla is voluntarily recalling Fosfomycin Tromethamine Granules for Oral Solution in the United States after the product failed to meet the required impurity and degradation standards, according to the latest enforcement report issued by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

The US FDA has classified the action as a Class II recall, indicating that the use of or exposure to the affected product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences. However, the probability of serious adverse health consequences is considered remote.

Fosfomycin Tromethamine Granules for Oral Solution is used for the treatment of acute uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs) in women. The recall was initiated after the product failed to comply with the prescribed impurity and degradation standards.

The recall is voluntary and applies to the product distributed in the US. The FDA's Class II classification indicates that the product may pose a risk of temporary or reversible health effects, although serious adverse health consequences are considered unlikely.

Cipla is undertaking the voluntary recall following the product's failure to meet the required impurity and degradation specifications. The total quantity of the recalled product has not been disclosed by Cipla.
